$comment: Routing and bindings for the task-orchestrator. The orchestrator reads this at dispatch time and passes `model` explicitly; agent frontmatter is only the fallback. A consuming repo overrides any key by writing .agents/orchestrator.json at its root; scripts/bindings.sh prints the merged result (repo values win, objects merge, arrays and scalars replace). Tiers keep the table readable: flip one phase between tiers here, never in an agent file.

scope.why: reads the tracker, plans the stack; small and needs the parent's judgment

implement.why: the only phase that writes product code

fix.why: same as implement, narrowed to one finding

verify.why: drives curl/Playwright and writes specs; the cheap tier drops flows mid-run

review.why: the final gate; Standards + Spec axes in one context

publish.why: gh stack submit is a host command; the prose work forks to the skill's pinned model (.claude/skill-models.json)

environments.$comment: Per phase: run | defer | no. `defer` records the phase as skipped with note `deferred:<env>`; resume.sh re-opens it in an environment that can run it. Detection: ORCH_ENV, else /sandbox => sandbox, else no docker => cloud, else local.

cloud.why: no local runtime or browser: verify needs the dev stack, so it is deferred; state is mirrored to refs/orchestrator/state because the clone dies with the session

sandbox.why: the worktree is a copy and git runs on the host, so nothing past review can happen here; download the copy and resume locally

gate.$comment: How many fix rounds a slice may spend before it is blocked and the run stops. A round is one fix dispatch + commit + fix-check. The cap counts rounds, not findings: one round may fix several. Override in the repo overlay.

envelope.nudge: Your envelope at {path} is {problem}. Write the complete envelope now as JSON to that exact path — every required field for phase {phase}, ending with "complete": true — then stop. Do not redo or extend the work; report only what you already did.

bindings.$comment: What the repo must tell the orchestrator. `required` lists the keys that must be non-null after the overlay; a missing one is stop-and-report, never a guess. `review_bot` is null (CI is the only gate) or an object {trigger, author, check, verdict, skip_on}: `trigger` is the command that asks the bot to review, posted once per layer whose class is not in `skip_on` (null = the bot reviews on its own); `author` is the GitHub login its reviews and threads carry; `check` is a status check that says the reviewer ran (optional); `verdict` is a check that must pass on HEAD (null = the latest review by `author` is on HEAD with no unresolved thread it opened). Whatever bot the repo uses, it is described here and never named in a skill. A label set to null in the overlay is dropped: that concern is not scoped in the repo.
